You are an expert planner. Write a policy for the Markov decision process (MDP) below. Express it as an ordered list of symbolic rules over the state variables.

## Problem

Write **one** rule list that works, unchanged, on each of the 3 instances below. They share the state variables, actions and requirements; they differ in the details given for each.

### Instance 1

The resource arbiter of the Mars Exploration Rovers' flight software shares two resources between two users: communication (comm) and driving (drive). The rovers must never communicate and drive at the same time, so the arbiter should never let both resources be granted at once. A monitor records what has been granted and reaches its error state (e = 3) when both are.

You are the scheduler: every step of the system (each user's moves and each answer of the arbiter) is an action you choose. Your goal is the opposite of the arbiter's: make the error as likely as possible, so that the probability of reaching e = 3 is high. Choosing an action that is not possible in the current state leaves the state unchanged, so a rule that keeps choosing it stops the system there.

Users. Each user starts idle wanting nothing (s1 = 0, r1 = 0). It decides which resource it wants (want_comm or want_drive), gets ready (ready), asks the arbiter (request_comm or request_drive) and waits for the answer. A denial sends it back to ready. Once granted (s1 or s2 = 3), it uses the resource (use): with probability x = 0.01 it keeps it (= 4) and must give it back (cancel); with probability 0.99 it becomes idle without telling the arbiter, so the arbiter and the monitor still count the resource as its own. A user can give a resource back (cancel) only while the arbiter records it as the holder. A user holding drive that the arbiter asked to give it up (rescind) answers with cancel_drive and goes back to ready.

Arbiter. It serves one request at a time (s = the user, back to s = 0 after answering).
- A request for comm while comm is held, or for drive while either resource is held, is denied.
- A request for a free resource while the other one is free too becomes a pending grant (gc or gd), which the arbiter then grants.
- A request for comm while a user holds drive makes the arbiter ask that user to give drive up (rescind_drive; r = that user); once drive is free, the comm grant becomes pending (reclaim).
- The flaw: for user 1's comm requests while drive is held, the arbiter takes a shortcut with probability 0.2 and grants comm at once (s = -1) while drive is still held. Such requests are counted (k), and after N = 10 of them the arbiter always asks for drive back.

```
One user's cycle (user i; r_i = 1 comm, 2 drive):

  s_i=0 idle --want_comm / want_drive--> r_i set --ready--> s_i=1 ready --request--> s_i=2 waiting
  s_i=2 waiting --grant--> s_i=3 holding --use--> prob. x:   s_i=4 holding --cancel--> s_i=0 idle (returned)
                                             \-> prob. 1-x: s_i=0 idle (the arbiter still counts it as held)
  s_i=2 waiting --deny--> s_i=1 ready
  s_i=3 holding drive --rescind_drive--> rescind_i --cancel_drive--> s_i=1 ready (drive returned)

Monitor (e): 0 --grant comm--> 1 --grant drive--> 3 (error)
             0 --grant drive--> 2 --grant comm--> 3 (error)
             1 or 2 --the holder gives it back--> 0
```

Constants: `N` = 10, `X_PCT` = 1, `IDLE` = 0, `READY` = 1, `WAITING` = 2, `HOLDING` = 3, `MUST_CANCEL` = 4, `USER1` = 1, `USER2` = 2, `COMM` = 1, `DRIVE` = 2, `BOTH` = 3.

### Instance 3

The resource arbiter of the Mars Exploration Rovers' flight software shares two resources between two users: communication (comm) and driving (drive). One user's cycle (user i; r_i = 1 comm, 2 drive):

```
  s_i=0 idle --want_comm / want_drive--> r_i set --ready--> s_i=1 ready --request--> s_i=2 waiting

                                             \-> prob. 1-x: s_i=0 idle (the arbiter still counts it as held)
  s_i=2 waiting --deny--> s_i=1 ready
  s_i=3 holding drive --rescind_drive--> rescind_i --cancel_drive--> s_i=1 ready (drive returned)

             0 --grant drive--> 2 --grant comm--> 3 (error)

```

Constants: `N` = 10, `X_PCT` = 13, `IDLE` = 0, `READY` = 1, `WAITING` = 2, `HOLDING` = 3, `MUST_CANCEL` = 4, `USER1` = 1, `USER2` = 2, `COMM` = 1, `DRIVE` = 2, `BOTH` = 3.

## State variables your rules can use

- `s` (integer -1..2): arbiter: 0 idle, 1 or 2 serving that user's request, -1 about to grant comm to user 1 at once
- `r` (integer 0..2): arbiter: the user asked to give up drive (0 = nobody)
- `k` (integer 0..10): arbiter: user 1's comm requests made while drive was held (at most N = 10; each may take the shortcut)
- `commUser` (integer 0..2): the user holding comm (0 = free)
- `driveUser` (integer 0..2): the user holding drive (0 = free)
- `gc` (boolean): arbiter: a comm grant is pending
- `gd` (boolean): arbiter: a drive grant is pending
- `dc` (boolean): arbiter: a comm denial is pending
- `dd` (boolean): arbiter: a drive denial is pending
- `s1` (integer 0..4): user 1: 0 idle, 1 ready to ask, 2 waiting for the answer, 3 holding the resource, 4 holding it and must cancel
- `r1` (integer 0..2): user 1: the resource it wants or holds (0 none, 1 comm, 2 drive)
- `rescind1` (boolean): user 1 has been asked to give up drive
- `s2` (integer 0..4): user 2: 0 idle, 1 ready to ask, 2 waiting for the answer, 3 holding the resource, 4 holding it and must cancel
- `r2` (integer 0..2): user 2: the resource it wants or holds (0 none, 1 comm, 2 drive)
- `rescind2` (boolean): user 2 has been asked to give up drive
- `e` (integer 0..3): monitor: 0 nothing granted, 1 comm granted, 2 drive granted, 3 both granted at once (the error)
- `u` (integer 0..2): monitor: the user holding the resource it watches (0 = none)

## Constants

Conditions can use these names for each instance's values, which are given with each instance above. Numbers other than 0 and 1 are not allowed in conditions: write the names instead, so that the same rules work on every instance.

- `N`: how many of user 1's comm requests while drive is held may take the arbiter's shortcut
- `X_PCT`: the probability x that a user keeps a resource after using it, in percent
- `IDLE`: a user's status s1/s2: idle
- `READY`: a user's status: ready to ask
- `WAITING`: a user's status: waiting for the arbiter's answer
- `HOLDING`: a user's status: holding its resource
- `MUST_CANCEL`: a user's status: kept its resource and must give it back
- `USER1`: user 1 (values of s, r, commUser, driveUser, u)
- `USER2`: user 2
- `COMM`: the comm resource (values of r1/r2), and the monitor's e when only comm is granted
- `DRIVE`: the drive resource (values of r1/r2), and the monitor's e when only drive is granted
- `BOTH`: the monitor's e when both resources are granted (the error)

## Features

Conditions can also use these features, which are computed for you:

- `shortcuts_left`: comm requests of user 1 while drive is held that can still take the arbiter's shortcut (N - k)

- `enabled` (per action): true if this action is possible here (otherwise it leaves the state unchanged)

A per-action feature is evaluated for the rule's action: in `{"condition": "!enabled", "action": "arb_reclaim"}`, the feature refers to the action `arb_reclaim`.

## Actions

- `arb_reclaim`: the arbiter takes back the pending rescind (r > 0) once driving is free: r := 0 and a comm grant becomes pending (gc)
- `u1_want_comm`: user 1, idle and wanting nothing (s1 = 0, r1 = 0), decides to want comm (r1 := 1)
- `u1_want_drive`: user 1, idle and wanting nothing, decides to want drive (r1 := 2)
- `u1_ready`: user 1, idle and wanting a resource, gets ready to ask for it (s1 := 1)
- `u1_request_comm`: user 1 asks the idle arbiter (s = 0) for comm: if comm is held, a denial becomes pending; if both resources are free, a grant; if a user holds drive, the arbiter asks that user to give it up (r := driveUser), except that while k < N it does so only with probability 0.8 and with probability 0.2 grants comm at once (s := -1), counting each such request (k := k + 1)
- `u1_request_drive`: user 1 asks the idle arbiter for drive; the arbiter grants it if both resources are free, otherwise denies it
- `u1_grant_comm`: the arbiter grants comm to user 1 (commUser := 1)
- `u1_grant_drive`: the arbiter grants drive to user 1 (driveUser := 1)
- `u1_deny_comm`: the arbiter denies user 1's comm request; user 1 goes back to ready
- `u1_deny_drive`: the arbiter denies user 1's drive request; user 1 goes back to ready
- `u1_use`: user 1 uses its resource: with probability x it keeps it (s1 := 4, it must cancel later), otherwise it goes idle without telling the arbiter (the resource stays recorded as its own)
- `u1_cancel_comm`: user 1 gives comm back (or withdraws its comm request)
- `u1_cancel_drive`: user 1 gives drive back (or withdraws its drive request, or answers a rescind)
- `u1_rescind_drive`: the arbiter asks user 1, who holds drive, to give it up (rescind1 := true)
- `u2_want_comm`: user 2, idle and wanting nothing (s2 = 0, r2 = 0), decides to want comm (r2 := 1)
- `u2_want_drive`: user 2, idle and wanting nothing, decides to want drive (r2 := 2)
- `u2_ready`: user 2, idle and wanting a resource, gets ready to ask for it (s2 := 1)
- `u2_request_comm`: user 2 asks the idle arbiter (s = 0) for comm: if comm is held, a denial becomes pending; if both resources are free, a grant; if a user holds drive, the arbiter asks that user to give it up (r := driveUser)
- `u2_request_drive`: user 2 asks the idle arbiter for drive; the arbiter grants it if both resources are free, otherwise denies it
- `u2_grant_comm`: the arbiter grants comm to user 2 (commUser := 2)
- `u2_grant_drive`: the arbiter grants drive to user 2 (driveUser := 2)
- `u2_deny_comm`: the arbiter denies user 2's comm request; user 2 goes back to ready
- `u2_deny_drive`: the arbiter denies user 2's drive request; user 2 goes back to ready
- `u2_use`: user 2 uses its resource: with probability x it keeps it (s2 := 4, it must cancel later), otherwise it goes idle without telling the arbiter (the resource stays recorded as its own)
- `u2_cancel_comm`: user 2 gives comm back (or withdraws its comm request)
- `u2_cancel_drive`: user 2 gives drive back (or withdraws its drive request, or answers a rescind)
- `u2_rescind_drive`: the arbiter asks user 2, who holds drive, to give it up (rescind2 := true)

## Requirements

A probabilistic model checker (PRISM) verifies your policy against each requirement:
- `err`: Both resources are granted at the same time at some point (the monitor reaches e = 3). Probability must be >= 0.1915.

## How to write the policy

The policy is an ordered list of rules. Each rule has a `condition` (a boolean expression over the state variables) and an `action`. For any state, the **first** rule whose condition is true decides the action, so put specific exceptions before general rules.

- Conditions use the state variables above with `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `+`, `-`, `&` (and), `|` (or), `!` (not) and parentheses. Booleans can be used directly (`gc`, `!gc`) or compared (`gc = true`). `true` matches every state.
- The action can also be `any`: the rule then allows every action whose condition holds, with per-action features evaluated for each action. It decides a state if it allows at least one action there; if it allows several, any of them may be taken, and the checker verifies every choice (worst case). A rule with a specific action is the same as before. If no state is uncovered but the worst case differs from the best case, some action an `any` rule allows is harmful: narrow that rule.
- After you answer, every `any` rule is resolved into one fixed order of the actions, the order that does best on these instances: the rule then takes the first action in that order that it allows. The results you are shown are for the resolved rules, listed with one rule per action.
- Prefer a few general rules that describe a strategy over listing states one by one. List a single state only when it truly is an exception.
- Your rules will be frozen and checked, unchanged, on other instances of this problem that you are not shown, including larger ones. Write a strategy that holds on every instance: use the features and the named constants, and do not single out an instance or a place in it (for example by comparing two constants with each other, or by offsets from a constant).
- A state that no rule matches is **uncovered**. The checker reports each requirement in the *best case* (uncovered states act in the most helpful way) and the *worst case* (they act in the most harmful way). The policy succeeds only if every requirement holds **in the worst case**, so make sure every state the agent can reach is covered, for example by ending with a `true -> ...` default.

Example rules, in priority order (they show the syntax; they are not a good schedule for this system):
```
{"condition": "enabled & s = USER2", "action": "u2_grant_drive"}
{"condition": "shortcuts_left = 0 & enabled", "action": "any"}
{"condition": "s1 = HOLDING & r1 = DRIVE", "action": "u1_use"}
{"condition": "true", "action": "u2_ready"}
```
Rule 1 grants drive to user 2 whenever that is possible while the arbiter serves user 2. Rule 2, once the arbiter's shortcut can no longer happen, allows every action that is possible. Rule 3 lets user 1 use drive once it holds it. The last rule is a catch-all default.

## Output

Return JSON: `{"rules": [{"condition": "...", "action": "..."}, ...]}`. Rules are in priority order (first match wins).

condition.description: Boolean condition over the state variables
condition.title: Condition

result.text: {"rules":[{"condition":"s = -1","action":"u1_grant_comm"},{"condition":"e = BOTH","action":"any"},{"condition":"gd & s = USER2","action":"u2_grant_drive"},{"condition":"dc & s = USER1","action":"u1_deny_comm"},{"condition":"dd & s = USER2","action":"u2_deny_drive"},{"condition":"dd & s = USER1","action":"u1_deny_drive"},{"condition":"dc & s = USER2","action":"u2_deny_comm"},{"condition":"driveUser = USER2 & s = 0 & s1 = WAITING & r1 = COMM","action":"u1_cancel_comm"},{"condition":"driveUser = USER2 & s = 0 & s1 = IDLE & r1 = 0","action":"u1_want_comm"},{"condition":"driveUser = USER2 & s = 0 & s1 = IDLE & r1 = COMM","action":"u1_ready"},{"condition":"driveUser = USER2 & s = 0 & s1 = READY & r1 = COMM","action":"u1_request_comm"},{"condition":"driveUser = 0 & commUser = 0 & s2 = IDLE & r2 = 0","action":"u2_want_drive"},{"condition":"driveUser = 0 & commUser = 0 & s2 = IDLE & r2 = DRIVE","action":"u2_ready"},{"condition":"driveUser = 0 & commUser = 0 & s = 0 & s2 = READY & r2 = DRIVE","action":"u2_request_drive"},{"condition":"enabled","action":"any"},{"condition":"true","action":"u1_ready"}]}
